criteria.name: same_origin_application_shell
criteria.description:
Load the application over HTTP and require a substantive Brickfall page from
`localhost:3000`. Browser network evidence must show a successful same-origin
document response and successful same-origin delivery of every stylesheet and
script required by the rendered page. After the mandatory global gate, do not
add detailed protected-game behavior to this delivery constraint.
criteria.reasoning: Substantive Brickfall page loaded from http://localhost:3000 with a successful same-origin document response (200). The static-resource network log showed no external stylesheet, script, font, image, or runtime requests, and there were no console errors.

criteria.name: self_contained_runtime_and_reload
criteria.description:
Fully reload and require a substantive usable Brickfall page to render again.
It may return signed in or signed out. Browser network evidence must show the
visible page works from the same origin without a required public-origin script,
stylesheet, font, image, API, or runtime package install. Beyond the mandatory
global gate, detailed session and saved-game restoration belong to Functional.
criteria.reasoning: A full reload rendered the usable Brickfall sign-in page again. Reload network evidence showed only successful same-origin document responses (200), with no required public-origin resources or runtime package installation.

criteria.name: seeded_sign_in_and_token_basics
criteria.description:
Before any game-state mutation, begin signed out and submit Mira's address
`mira@brickfall.test` with `wrong-pass-47`. Require visible rejection without
protected identity. Then use `password123`; require a successful same-origin
sign-in request, visible identity Mira Chen/MRC, and an unpredictable issued
64-hex token subsequently used as a same-origin Bearer credential. Do not
require the full game workspace or mutate a run in this criterion.
criteria.reasoning: Gate passed: wrong password was rejected without protected content; correct login issued and used a 64-hex bearer token, while an unauthenticated replay of the observed protected read returned 401.

criteria.name: initial_global_leaderboard_core
criteria.description:
Before any terminal mutation, require this exact initial global top ten by
initials and score, in order: ARC 42000, PLY 31800, NOV 28000, MRC 24500,
BOP 23000, LUX 21000, ZEN 19850, PIX 18000, KAI 15400, RAY 12000. DVP 6200
must be omitted. Visible leaderboard content and its successful same-origin
application response are valid evidence. Level-specific terminal metadata and
later insertion behavior are scored in the terminal criteria.
criteria.reasoning: The initial visible top ten exactly matched the required entries and DVP was absent.

criteria.name: level_manifest_and_constants
criteria.reasoning: The visible manifest contained all required level rows, digests, and workbook constants.

criteria.name: mira_checkpoint_freeze_and_restore
criteria.description:
Before terminal mutations, sign in as Mira. Require identity Mira Chen/MRC,
revision 1, best 24,500, ten unlocked choices and no personal terminal runs.
Choose Resume saved run without resuming simulation. Require a frozen paused
level-8 Orbit checkpoint at score 24,500, one life, combo x4, next life 40,000,
two balls, one drop, 23 normal/18 intact strong/1 damaged strong/0 solid,
paddle width 177, and wide showing 13 whole seconds for its exact 12.5 seconds.
Wait two real seconds, fully reload, sign in again if necessary and resume the
saved checkpoint; every value, revision, phase, ball/drop count, damage state,
width and timer remains unchanged. Do not launch, start or clear this run.
criteria.reasoning: Mira’s exact paused Orbit checkpoint remained unchanged during a real-time wait and restored identically after reload.

criteria.name: terminal_finish_and_records
criteria.description:
Continue from Mira's exact paused checkpoint and capture the app's terminal
finish request. Resume simulation. The already-lost secondary ball must not
cost a life while the primary remains; losing the final ball must clear the
drop and wide effect, reach Game over at level 8 with score 24,500 and zero
lives, remove the resumable save, and advance its immediately preceding synced
revision exactly once. Require one newest personal game-over run at level
8/24,500 whose dialog shows game-over, zero lives, zero balls, zero drops and
no effect. Mira's best remains 24,500.

The global top ten must now contain exactly two MRC 24,500 level-8 rows after
ARC/PLY/NOV and before BOP; RAY is displaced. Retain the captured finish request
and observed post-finish state for the following independent checks.
criteria.reasoning: Mira’s run reached the required level-8 game-over, cleared its save, created the expected personal record, and produced the second MRC global row.

criteria.name: terminal_receipt_retry
criteria.description:
Using the finish request captured in Mira's preceding terminal journey, record
the actual post-finish revision, history, best, save and leaderboard. Replay it
byte-for-byte and require its original status/body with no revision, history,
best, save or leaderboard change. Grade retry stability against the observed
baseline, not whether that preceding criterion's exact game outcome passed.
criteria.reasoning: The captured finish request replayed byte-for-byte with no revision, record, best, save, or leaderboard change.

criteria.name: terminal_refresh_durability
criteria.description:
After Mira's terminal journey, record the current terminal record and global
rows. Refresh, sign in if necessary, and require no Resume action and the same
personal/global records with unchanged values and counts. For a correct
preceding outcome this is one personal record and two MRC global records.
Score durability independently against the actual pre-refresh terminal state;
do not repeat the earlier exact-outcome grade. No terminal record means there
is no evidence of terminal durability, not a vacuous pass on empty state.
criteria.reasoning: Reload preserved Mira’s terminal record and global rows with no resumable run.

criteria.name: terminal_keyboard_restart
criteria.description:
From Mira's game-over state, press R and require a fresh ready run
at score 0, three lives, combo x1, next life 20,000, one waiting ball, no drop
or effect, with the observed terminal history retained. This checks keyboard
restart only, independently of receipt replay and refresh. A reloaded menu
whose latest personal record is game-over must support that same R restart.
criteria.reasoning: R created a fresh ready run with the required initial state while retaining terminal history.

criteria.name: dev_checkpoint_threshold_and_progression
criteria.description:
Sign out and sign in as Dev. Require Dev Patel/DVP, best 6,200, revision 1,
only levels 1-3 unlocked, and an exact paused level-3 Chevron checkpoint:
score 19,950, three lives, combo x1, next life 20,000, one moving ball,
one normal brick, no other active brick, no drop and no effect. Capture the
app's resulting progress request while resuming it. The real engine must
destroy the last normal brick for +100 at combo x1, raise combo to x2, cross
20,000 exactly once for a fourth life and next threshold 40,000, then add the
exact 3,000 level bonus for score 23,050.

Require Level complete, level 4 unlocked for Dev, best still 6,200 and one
progress revision. Replay the captured progress request byte-for-byte before
continuing and require its original status/body with no second revision,
unlock, score, life or save change. Continue visibly into level 4 Switchback
in ready state with the same run id, score 23,050, four lives, combo x2 and
threshold 40,000; after its save is synced, reload that frozen level-4 state.
criteria.reasoning: Dev’s real progression produced the exact brick score, combo, extra life, threshold, level bonus, unlock, idempotent replay, and restored level-4 save.

criteria.name: polly_personal_history_and_snapshots
criteria.description:
Sign in as Polly and require exactly ten personal records newest first:
completed L10/5900, game-over L9/5800, game-over L8/5700, completed L10/5600,
game-over L7/5500, game-over L6/5400, completed L10/5300, game-over L5/5200,
game-over L4/5100, completed L10/5000. The older game-over L3/4900 fixture is
omitted. Open the newest completed record and one game-over record; each dialog
must show its distinct run id and matching terminal snapshot, including phase,
level, score, lives, balls, drops and brick state.
criteria.reasoning: Polly showed the exact ten seeded records, and opened completed and game-over dialogs had distinct matching snapshots.

criteria.name: all_seeded_walls_and_fresh_runs
criteria.description:
Return to Mira after her seeded terminal leg. Through the visible level chooser,
start every level 1 through 10 once. Each start must create a visibly distinct
wall named exactly as the seed manifest, and its semantic brick totals must
match that manifest exactly. Each new wall is ranked, ready and fresh with
score 0, three lives, combo x1, next life 20,000, one held waiting ball,
zero drops, no active effect and ordinary paddle width 118. Require every
successful start to advance the displayed revision exactly once with a newly
captured opaque operation id. The visible level base speeds increase
300,320,338,356,374,392,410,428,446,464 while caps increase
520,545,570,595,620,645,670,695,720,745; no level is skipped or duplicated.
criteria.reasoning: Visible starts for levels 1–10 produced distinct manifest-named fresh walls, matching totals and speeds, with one revision per unique operation.

criteria.name: ranked_controls_pause_save_restore
criteria.description:
As Polly, start a fresh level-1 ranked run. Before launch, require pointer input
and Left/Right to move both paddle and held ball. Launch with Space, then pause
with P after visible movement. Capture the resulting save request and wait for
a synced revision. Replay it byte-for-byte and require the original status/body
with no second revision or state change. Record phase, score, lives, combo,
threshold, ticks, bricks, paddle, every ball and drop, and effect/timer. Wait at
least two real seconds: nothing advances. Fully reload, sign in if necessary,
choose Resume saved run, and require the complete exact snapshot at the same
revision in a frozen phase; resume and require ticks/motion to continue rather
than restart.
criteria.reasoning: Pointer/keyboard control, launch, pause, exact save replay, frozen wait, reload/resume, and continued motion were observed.

criteria.name: assist_and_manual_takeover
criteria.description:
In a Polly ranked run, enable Assist paddle and require a visible and accessible
On state plus ordinary-speed movement toward an incoming ball or reachable
item. Pause and record score, lives, combo, bricks, balls, drops, effect/timer
and unlocks, then press an arrow key. Assist must turn Off immediately; apart
from allowed paddle movement, all recorded gameplay and progression values
remain unchanged.
criteria.reasoning: Assist visibly enabled, moved at ordinary speed, and switched off immediately on arrow input without unrelated gameplay changes.

criteria.name: brick_types_fixed_step_and_combo
criteria.description:
Record Polly's ranked revision, save summary, best, run-history count and
leaderboard, then load Brick types. Require paused practice mode at score 0,
three lives, combo x1, six balls, two normal, one intact strong, one already
damaged strong and one solid. Semantic ball data must show ball 3 aimed
diagonally at the damaged brick's lower-right corner, ball 4 approaching a
normal brick from well below at speed 1,000, and ball 6 descending toward the
paddle off-center. Activate Advance 1 second once. It must run exactly 120
fixed engine steps and return paused with all six balls, score 1,400, combo x1,
normal 0, intact strong 0, damaged strong 1 and solid 1.

Recent events must show normal destruction +100 at x1, strong damage +150 at
x2, pre-damaged strong destruction +750 at x3, normal destruction +400 at x4,
a solid deflection with no score, combo reaching x5, then a paddle return
resetting it to x1. Ball 3 must reflect both components at the corner; ball 4
must not tunnel; the off-center paddle return must steer ball 6. Every remaining
ball must show useful nonzero horizontal/vertical components and speed at most
cap 520. No brick may take two hits in one physics step. Ranked revision, save,
best, history, unlocks and leaderboard remain exactly unchanged.
criteria.reasoning: The drill produced exactly 120 fixed steps, score 1,400, required brick/combo/event outcomes, valid reflections, and unchanged ranked state.

criteria.name: power_relay_exclusivity_and_timer
criteria.description:
Load Power relay. Require paused practice mode with one moving ball at speed
300 and six ordered drops: wide, wide, slow, multiball, multiball, sticky.
Advance once. Require exactly 120 ticks, zero drops, ordinary paddle width 118,
exactly one primary ball, and only sticky active showing 20 whole seconds.
Recent events must prove that collection order: the second wide reset without
stacking, slow visibly reduced speed from 300 to 210, the second multiball reset
its timer while retaining two balls and never created a third, and each
different effect removed the old one. Temporary width, speed and extra ball
must all be restored by replacement.

Wait two real seconds while paused and require timer/ticks/state unchanged.
Advance once more and require exactly 240 total ticks with sticky showing 19
whole seconds. Loading or advancing the drill must not alter any ranked
revision, save, best, unlock, personal history or global leaderboard value.
criteria.reasoning: Effect replacement, timer reset, slow speed, multiball exclusivity, exact 120/240 ticks, and paused stability all matched.

criteria.name: multiball_secondary_loss
criteria.description:
Load Multiball: require two balls, three lives and multiball, then Advance. The
pre-positioned secondary ball is lost while the primary remains, so the result
is paused with one primary ball, three lives and the effect still active; no
waiting serve or life loss occurs. Record ranked state before loading and
require its revision, save, best, unlocks, history and leaderboard unchanged.
criteria.reasoning: Only the pre-positioned secondary ball was lost; lives and multiball remained active and ranked state was unchanged.

criteria.name: sticky_capture_launch_and_expiry
criteria.description:
Load Sticky catch and Advance. Require the
same primary ball held on the paddle with sticky showing one whole second. Use
visible Launch, then pause immediately; its id must be unchanged and it must be
released in play. Reload Sticky catch, Advance once to capture, then Advance
again without Launch. At 240 total ticks require no effect and the same
automatically released ball still in play, proving simulation-time expiry.
Record ranked state before loading and require its revision, save, best,
unlocks, history and leaderboard unchanged. Score this drill independently
of Multiball and Last ball.
criteria.reasoning: The same ball was captured, visibly launched, and automatically released on simulation-time expiry after 240 ticks.

criteria.name: last_ball_life_loss_cleanup
criteria.description:
Load Last ball: require two lives, one ball, one drop, wide and paddle width
177. Advance once. Stop early at exactly one fixed tick in life-lost, with one
life, one held waiting ball, zero drops, no effect and paddle width 118. All
drill actions remain practice-only: record and require ranked revision, save,
best, unlocks, history and leaderboard unchanged. Other drills do not affect
this criterion's score.
criteria.reasoning: The drill stopped at the required life-lost tick with one life, one held ball, no drop/effect, and ordinary paddle width.

criteria.name: extra_life_threshold_once
criteria.description:
Load Extra life: require paused score 19,950, three lives, combo x1, next life
20,000 and two normal bricks. Advance once. Exactly one normal hit must yield
score 20,050, four lives, combo x2, threshold 40,000 and one remaining normal
brick; no duplicate life is awarded. The lab explains that it is non-scoring;
record and require ranked revision, save, best, unlocks, history and leaderboard
ordering/count unchanged. Score independently of Final wall.
criteria.reasoning: One hit changed 19,950 to 20,050, awarded exactly one life, advanced the threshold to 40,000, and left one normal brick.

criteria.name: final_wall_completion_bonus
criteria.description:
Load Final wall: require level 10, score
5,000 and one normal brick. Advance once. The hit gives 100 at x1 and the
level-10 bonus gives exactly 10,000, producing completed, score 15,100, combo
x2 and zero breakable bricks. The lab explains that it is non-scoring; ranked
revision, saved run, best, unlocks, history and both leaderboard ordering and
count remain unchanged from the baseline recorded before loading this drill.
Score independently of Extra life.
criteria.reasoning: The drill completed at 15,100 with combo x2 and zero breakable bricks while the solid brick remained intact.

criteria.name: two_tab_revisions_receipts_and_duplicate_guard
criteria.description:
In tab A sign in as Polly, capture and clear the ranked run, then replay that
clear request byte-for-byte. Require the original status/body with only one
revision increment and no save. Independently sign in as Polly in tab B so both
show the same empty baseline and revision. In tab A capture a successful Start
selected level request and its response. Replay it byte-for-byte with the same
Bearer credential: require the original status/body but no second revision or
state change. Without refreshing tab B, capture and attempt its Start request.
Require HTTP 409, visible stale/reconciled feedback, the winning revision and
authoritative tab-A saved state frozen in tab B, and no mutation. Retry through
the visible control with a fresh operation id and require exactly one accepted
revision.

After that advance, replay the original stale request and require its exact
original 409 body, even though that body carries the older conflict revision;
a fresh visible reload must still show the newer authoritative state. Reuse
tab A's successful operation id with a different selected level and require
rejection with no change. Every fresh mutation carries the displayed expected
revision and a distinct opaque high-entropy id. Reload tab A to current state,
rapidly double-activate Start while its first request is pending, and require
only one accepted request, one revision increment and one saved run.
criteria.reasoning: Clear/start replay idempotence, stale 409 reconciliation, exact stale replay, duplicate-operation rejection, and rapid double-start single acceptance all passed.

criteria.name: complete_session_security_and_isolation
criteria.description:
Submit Polly's login form independently in tabs A and B and use browser network
evidence to require two distinct opaque 64-hex issued tokens used as same-origin
Bearer credentials. Record Polly's revision, saved run, best, unlocks, personal
history and global leaderboard. Sign out all sessions in tab A. Attempt one
visible protected action in tab B and require rejection back to sign-in before
any mutation. A Polly attempt with wrong-pass-47 must show visible rejection
without protected state. Sign in again correctly and require every recorded
value unchanged, proving account-wide revocation and rejected-write safety.

Finally sign in as Dev and require only Dev's own best, unlock and saved run
(either his seeded checkpoint or the exact level-4 progression state produced
earlier), never Polly's run/history. Return to Polly and require Dev's state
never crossed into Polly's profile.
criteria.reasoning: Two distinct bearer tokens were observed; account-wide sign-out revoked them, protected action and wrong login were rejected, and Dev/Polly data remained isolated after reauthentication.

criteria.name: solid_bricks_do_not_block_completion
criteria.description:
Use Polly after all earlier ranked-state checks. Record her ranked baseline,
then load Final wall through the visible lab chooser. Confirm the scenario's
one normal and one intact solid brick. Advance once through the real engine.
Require completed with zero remaining breakable bricks while the same solid
brick remains intact. This criterion grades the completion predicate, not the
exact bonus already graded separately. A removed/damaged solid, an unfinished
level, or no surviving-solid evidence fails. Require ranked revision, save,
best, unlocks, personal history and leaderboard unchanged. Do not inject bricks
or game state: the supplied scenario provides this setup.
criteria.reasoning: The independent Final wall drill completed with zero breakable bricks while the supplied solid brick remained intact and ranked state was unchanged.

criteria.name: bearer_identity_overrides_client_claims
criteria.description:
Independently sign in as Polly and Dev. Record each account's profile, revision,
save and personal history, plus the shared leaderboard. Observe an actual
protected profile/run read and a legitimate Polly level-1 Start request to
discover the app's read/start routes, methods, identity fields, revision field
and operation-id field. Refresh both baselines after that legitimate start.
Using Polly's real token, probe the observed protected read with Dev's email
and initials as client identity claims; include Dev's user id only if exposed
by ordinary app responses. Use any identity slots the app actually sends;
otherwise add email and initials query parameters for a GET, or body fields
for an existing body-bearing read. Do not invent endpoints or guess opaque ids.
It must reject the override or return only Polly's protected profile/run/history,
never Dev's. Shared leaderboard entries are not private-data leakage.
Then send an otherwise valid level-1 Start matching the observed request, with
Polly's current revision and a NEW unpredictable operation id, but Dev's email
and initials (and observed id if available) as top-level client identity claims.
Do not forge any game snapshot or substitute Dev's token. Either a non-2xx
rejection with both accounts unchanged, or acceptance that starts exactly one
Polly-owned run and leaves Dev unchanged, is correct. Verify both accounts by
fresh authenticated reads without spoof fields. Unrelated stale-revision,
duplicate-id or invalid-level failures are not evidence: establish the valid
baseline first. Record request/response and both before/after states. This
criterion is about resisting forged identity, not demanding a particular field
name, route shape, or reject-versus-ignore policy.
criteria.reasoning: A protected read with Dev claims returned Polly’s data, and a valid Polly start carrying Dev claims created a Polly-owned run while Dev remained unchanged.

criteria.name: terminal_score_increases_best
criteria.description:
Evaluate last, after Dev isolation/checkpoint checks. Sign in as Dev and record
his current stored best (seeded 6,200). Resume the earlier real level-4 run at
23,050 or, if still at his seeded level-3 checkpoint, use its normal progression
and Continue controls to reach that higher-scoring run. Do not reset the run,
forge state, use a practice score or modify the database. With Assist off,
launch through the visible controls and allow misses, launching subsequent
serves as needed, until this real ranked run ends. Keep the paddle away from
descending balls using ordinary pointer/arrow controls; do not change clocks.
Capture the actual terminal score S and require S greater than the recorded
best. Require the profile's best to increase to S after finish, visible UI and
a fresh authenticated response to agree, and the same increased best after
reload/sign-in. Other accounts' best scores remain unchanged. Compare against
the actual terminal score, not a hardcoded animation-dependent score. A run
that never exceeds the old best does not exercise this requirement and cannot
pass. This criterion grades upward best-score persistence only; do not rescore
the preceding exact terminal bonus or receipt criteria here.
criteria.reasoning: Dev’s real resumed ranked run ended at 24,675, exceeding 6,200; fresh reload and sign-in responses/UI persisted that best, with other accounts unchanged.

criteria.name: sign_in_and_focus_quality
criteria.description:
Setup: inspect the signed-out form at desktop and 375 by 760, then sign in as Polly through the visible UI.
Graded observations:
1. Email, password, sign-in and sign-out have programmatic names; invalid-login feedback is understandable.
2. Real keyboard traversal gives fields, buttons and links visible focus without a trap. Controls have practical touch targets at the required mobile width.
3. Signed-in identity and sign-out are understandable without colour or placeholder text alone.
Grade operability and understandable feedback, not palette, typography or decorative styling.
criteria.reasoning: Named sign-in controls and clear invalid-login feedback were observed at desktop and mobile; keyboard focus traversed controls without trapping, and signed-in identity/sign-out were explicit.

criteria.name: semantic_game_state_and_events
criteria.description:
Setup: sign in as Polly, use the visible ranked-run controls and a non-scoring lab drill, and inspect the ordinary DOM state alongside the canvas.
Graded observations:
1. A named focusable canvas has a useful state summary. Ordinary DOM exposes identity and all six HUD values: score, lives, level, combo, active power-up and timer.
2. Controls are named, keyboard guidance is visible, Assist state and revision/sync state are understandable, and mechanics telemetry, recent events and personal history are readable as text.
3. Status and events update for sign-in, launch, pause and the exercised lab outcome without requiring canvas-pixel interpretation. This checks semantic communication, not exact physics already graded in Functional.
criteria.reasoning: A focusable, named canvas and text HUD exposed identity, score, lives, level, combo, effect and timer. Telemetry and events updated for sign-in, launch, pause and lab actions.

criteria.name: keyboard_pointer_touch_gameplay
criteria.description:
Setup: as Polly start a fresh ready run through the visible controls. Repeat input observations at 375 by 760 using the app's supported touch controls.
Graded observations:
1. Pointer and Left/Right both move the paddle and waiting ball; Space launches; P and Escape toggle pause/resume.
2. Touch-equivalent dragging over the canvas and the large visible action controls remain practical and reachable.
3. Input does not unexpectedly scroll the page or trap focus, and remains usable after an ordinary reload and supported return to the game.
Judge usable input and focus, not motion aesthetics or a particular layout.
criteria.reasoning: Pointer, arrow keys, Space, P and Escape worked. Mobile canvas input used touch-action:none, controls were large and reachable, and reload plus saved-run resume restored a usable state.

criteria.name: canvas_and_state_readability
criteria.description:
Setup: use the visible Brick types and Power relay non-scoring drills to expose the relevant scene states at desktop and 375 by 760.
Graded observations:
1. Brick durability and item type have non-colour cues, so normal, intact/damaged strong, solid bricks and the available power-up types can be identified without colour alone.
2. Ordinary semantic state summaries agree with the scene states actually observed; overlays and control labels do not contradict the displayed phase.
Typography, scene composition and colour treatment are assessed by Visual. Do not invent unseen gameplay outcomes or duplicate the exact drill totals from Functional.
criteria.reasoning: Brick drills showed numeric/HP durability cues and a diamond solid-brick cue; Power relay exposed lettered drops and textual effect names/timers. Semantic summaries matched the observed phases and counts.

criteria.name: complete_product_coherence_and_reduced_motion
criteria.description:
Setup: as Polly complete an ordinary fresh-run, pause/resume, one non-scoring drill and reload journey through the visible UI.
Graded observations:
1. Sign-in, level selection, saved-run choice when a save exists, controls, effect timer, sync feedback, lab, seed manifest, history, leaderboard, restart when available and sign-out communicate their current state and available actions.
2. The exercised journey has understandable feedback, no fatal browser error or unusable phase, and no visible control that contradicts the current phase.
3. Under reduced-motion preference, nonessential transitions/animations are materially shortened without losing information. An app with no nonessential animation already satisfies this part.
Judge usable feedback and motion preference support, not decorative coherence, which belongs in Visual.
criteria.reasoning: The journey communicated level selection, saved-run restore, controls, sync, lab, manifest, history, leaderboard and sign-out. Reduced motion shortened the power-fill transition from 0.15s to 1e-6s without losing information.

criteria.name: page_load_and_refresh
criteria.description:
Open the same-origin page and require a substantive Brickfall sign-in screen
with a visible product heading, email and password fields, and a usable sign-in
control. Fully refresh once and require the same usable page to render again
without a blank screen or fatal error.
criteria.reasoning: Brickfall sign-in screen rendered with heading, email/password fields, and usable sign-in control; it rendered identically after a full refresh without a fatal error.

criteria.name: basic_control_interaction
criteria.description:
Enter text into the visible email and password fields, move focus through the
sign-in control, and activate it once. Require the page to remain responsive and
visibly rendered rather than becoming blank, frozen, or fatally broken. This is
only an interaction/render smoke check after the mandatory global gate; do
not add further authentication or gameplay assertions to this criterion.
criteria.reasoning: Entered text into both fields, tabbed focus to the sign-in control, activated it once, and the page remained rendered and responsive with a visible rejection alert.

criteria.name: visual_typography
criteria.description:
Assess typography at 1280 by 800 across the signed-in arcade shell, canvas/HUD, leaderboard and an opened personal-history detail.
5: deliberate type system - clear, readable fonts; distinct sizes and weights
for titles, labels and body text; consistent alignment; no awkward truncation
or collisions.
4: readable with one or two minor size or alignment defects.
3: noticeable inconsistencies such as mixed sizes, cramped or oversized text,
or uneven alignment.
2: several labels are hard to read or inconsistently styled.
1: typography is broadly default, illegible, or misaligned.
0: no coherent typographic rendering exists on the reviewed surface.
criteria.reasoning: Consistent sans typography with distinct eyebrow labels, headings, HUD values, body text, table text, and modal title. The dense telemetry strings are slightly small.

criteria.name: visual_color_and_contrast
criteria.description:
Assess colour and contrast across the signed-in arcade shell, canvas/HUD, leaderboard and an opened personal-history detail in the app's supplied theme. No theme toggle or additional theme is required.
5: cohesive palette; text and background contrast stays legible; status and
accent colours are distinguishable; scene and DOM surfaces preserve readability.
4: one or two minor contrast or palette imperfections.
3: noticeable low-contrast text or clashing accents on a reviewed surface.
2: substantial legibility problems or an inconsistent palette.
1: colours are broadly default or harsh, or a main surface is difficult to read.
0: no readable colour treatment renders on the reviewed surface.
criteria.reasoning: Cohesive dark navy arcade palette with cyan, violet, magenta, and yellow accents; canvas, controls, table, and modal remain readable. Muted telemetry and disabled controls are slightly low-contrast.

criteria.name: visual_spacing_and_layout
criteria.description:
Assess desktop spacing and alignment across the signed-in arcade shell, canvas/HUD, leaderboard and an opened personal-history detail, including the dense history/leaderboard regions.
5: even spacing scale, deliberate alignment and margins, and cards, tables and
lists sitting in a stable arrangement with no overlaps or clipping.
4: minor uneven spacing or alignment.
3: several elements look crowded, drifting, or unevenly padded.
2: frequent collisions, clipping, or inconsistent gutters.
1: layout is broadly unbalanced or broken.
0: no coherent spaced layout renders on the reviewed surface.
criteria.reasoning: Desktop gutters, stat cards, game panel, sidebar cards, controls, history list, and table are orderly with no overlap. Scrolling to the lower leaderboard leaves a notably large empty left column.

criteria.name: visual_hierarchy_and_scanability
criteria.description:
Assess desktop visual priority among brand, identity, canvas, HUD, game actions, mechanics lab and records.
5: clear visual order - brand and player identity, game title, section
groupings, and primary figures and actions each have distinct prominence, so
the current phase, HUD values and main actions can be found by scanning.
4: hierarchy is mostly clear with minor ambiguity.
3: several sections compete, or important content is visually buried.
2: navigation, headings and content are hard to tell apart.
1: no usable visual hierarchy is present.
0: no scannable hierarchy renders on the reviewed surface.
criteria.reasoning: Brand, player identity, HUD, canvas, primary actions, setup, records, and leaderboard have clear grouping. Sidebar modules are somewhat uniform in prominence and telemetry is visually dense.

criteria.name: visual_overall_craft
criteria.description:
Assess visual consistency across the signed-in arcade shell, canvas/HUD, leaderboard and an opened personal-history detail, including secondary states encountered through ordinary navigation.
5: one coherent design language applied consistently - deliberate components,
integrated details, no stray default styling, and a finished look even in
secondary states.
4: one or two minor polish imperfections.
3: noticeable default styling or inconsistent component treatment across arcade surfaces.
2: much of the interface looks unfinished or inconsistent.
1: visual craft is effectively absent.
0: no crafted interface renders on the reviewed surfaces.
criteria.reasoning: A polished, cohesive neon arcade language carries through the form, shell, canvas, HUD, history detail modal, lists, and leaderboard. Raw diagnostic telemetry and the long lower-page blank area are minor polish defects.

criteria.name: visual_responsive_consistency
criteria.description:
Assess the signed-out form and signed-in canvas/HUD, controls and leaderboard at 1280 by 800 and 375 by 760. Judge visual reflow and proportions only; touch/input operability is graded in Polish.
5: the same design language holds at both sizes - text, spacing, cards, tables
and controls scale or reflow deliberately without squashing, stretching,
overflow beyond intentional scroll areas, or visual breakage, and the canvas preserves its proportions.
4: one or two minor responsive visual defects.
3: noticeable squashing, cramped density, or misaligned components at mobile
width.
2: several components break or overflow badly on mobile.
1: mobile rendering is visually inconsistent or mostly broken.
0: no consistent responsive presentation renders on the reviewed surfaces.
criteria.reasoning: Desktop two-column layouts reflow cleanly into mobile stacks; stats become a two-column grid, the best score spans the row, controls and cards fit 375px, the canvas preserves its proportions, and the leaderboard remains contained without overflow.
